canonical_data: a single encrypted local vault file with an in-memory hybrid vector/keyword index
strengths: Fully local, encrypted-at-rest vault (XChaCha20-Poly1305, Argon2id) with no account, API key, or network calls
Broad MCP client support - Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, VS Code - with one-command integration
Explicit per-claim provenance, expiry, and supersession logic rather than an opaque memory blob
weaknesses: Repository created about two months before this review (2026-07-20); no long-term adoption track record despite rapid star growth
Its own README carries a self-authored comparison table judging competing memory servers, uncorroborated by those projects
Fixed-tier importance heuristic (0.90/0.80/0.75/0.55/0.20) is a simple rule set, not a reasoning-based memory model
why_it_matters: A clean, self-contained illustration of encrypted, fully local, cross-client agent memory reachable from any MCP tool, though it is too new to show durability.
